newsitem.title: USA: Hilton says strong earnings will boost ITT bid.
newsitem.headline: Hilton says strong earnings will boost ITT bid.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp. Wednesday reported solid gains in first quarter earnings due to acquisitions that it said would bolster its $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid for ITT Corp.

Hilton's first quarter net income of $65 million, or 26 cents per share, roundly beat the year ago quarter's net income of $37 million, or 19 cents per share, and also topped financial analysts' forecasts of 23 cents a share.
Quarterly revenues rose to $1.3 billion from $957 million, led by full-service hotel operations and its $3 billion acquisition of Bally Entertainment Corp., completed in December.
Shares of the Beverly Hills-based company, the nation's largest hotel and gambling concern, rose $1.125 to $26.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Hilton seized on gains from the Bally merger and six hotels recently bought from The Prudential Insurance Co. to reinforce its belief that the proposed $6.5 billion acquisition of ITT would enhance the two companies' value.

"Our offer to acquire ITT...represents another unique opportunity for the shareholders of both companies," Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach said in a statment. "And we are on track for what we are confident will be a successful conclusion."
But Hilton's $55 per share cash and stock offer was effectively put on hold Monday when a federal judge in Las Vegas denied Hilton's motion to force an ITT shareholder vote on the proposed deal.

Hilton now must wait until New York-based ITT, owner of the Sheraton hotels and Caesars casinos, calls an annual meeting which could be as late as mid-November. In the meantime, ITT is shedding non-core assets to defend against Hilton.

On the earnings front, Hilton's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization rose 41 percent to $111 million from $79 million last year, reflecting strong results at upscale properties.
Overall hotel occupancy was up slightly to 71.8 percent versus 71.6 percent last year while average daily room rate rose eight percent to $146.
In the gambling division, Bally's hotels helped boost cash flow, which is earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, to $133 million from $54 million in 1996's first quarter.
Also, at the Las Vegas Hilton high-rolling baccarat card games helped its cash flow improve to $19 million from $1.0 million last year.
